primary_outcome_name: Psychological General Well-Being Index (PGWBI) global score
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: PGWBI global score, 22 items summed, range 0-110 (higher = better psychological well-being)
primary_timepoint: late pregnancy (gestational week 34-37); also assessed at 3 months postpartum
population_detail: Overweight/obese pregnant women (prepregnancy BMI >=28 kg/m2), included at gestational week 12-18; 91 women randomised (age 31.2+/-4.1 years, BMI 34.5+/-4.2 kg/m2), 46 exercise, 45 control. Secondary analysis of the ETIP (Exercise Training in Pregnancy) trial.

published_estimate.quote: Table 2, PGWBI row, 'Difference between groups', Late pregnancy: 'Diff 2.60 ... 95% CI −3.77 to 8.97 ... P value 0.42' (Table 2, BMJ Open 2019;9:e028252, p.6). Consistent with Abstract Results: 'Late pregnancy PGWBI; exercise 76.6 (95% CI 72.2 to 81.0), control 74.0 (95% CI 69.4 to 78.5) (p=0.42).' (Abstract, p.1). Table 2 also reports the postpartum comparison: 'Diff 0.77 ... 95% CI −4.42 to 5.95 ... P value 0.77.'

B_covariate_list: Baseline PGWBI score used as covariate for the late-pregnancy ANCOVA; late-pregnancy PGWBI score used as covariate for the postpartum ANCOVA ('Baseline values of each outcome were set as covariates in late pregnancy analyses, and late pregnancy values were set as covariates in postpartum analyses.'). No other covariates (e.g. BMI, age) reported for the primary PGWBI comparisons. For EPDS specifically, no covariates were used at all (plain independent-samples t-test on the postpartum value only).
data_availability_statement: Data availability statement Data file are being available in Dryad, doi:10.5061/dryad.pvmcvdng6.

registry_check.issues: 1) outcome_var=EPDS_total does NOT match this paper's (abstract-)first-named / most-emphasised outcome: the paper never formally labels a single 'primary outcome' variable for this secondary-analysis report; its abstract heading 'Primary and secondary outcomes measures' actually describes ITT (primary) vs per-protocol (secondary) ANALYSIS POPULATIONS, not an outcome hierarchy. Two outcome domains are named as aims: (a) psychological well-being (PGWBI, late pregnancy and 3-months postpartum) and (b) postnatal depression (EPDS). PGWBI is named first in the Abstract Objectives, described in far greater methodological detail, analysed via a pre-specified baseline-adjusted ANCOVA, and reported first in Results/Discussion; EPDS/postnatal depression is presented as an additional/secondary aim within this paper. We therefore coded PGWBI as the primary outcome per the task's default rule (first-named in abstract), which means outcome_var=EPDS_total in the registry targets what this paper treats as a secondary outcome, not its main one. 2) baseline_var=(empty) for EPDS is actually consistent with the paper: no EPDS baseline mean/SD/n is reported anywhere (Methods, Results, Tables, Figures) for either arm; the only EPDS numbers given are single post-values at 3 months postpartum (exercise 2.96, 95% CI 1.7-4.2; control 3.48, 95% CI 2.3-4.7; p=0.55), compared with a plain independent-samples t-test with NO baseline adjustment ('We analysed differences between groups in EPDS using an independent samples t-test.') - unlike PGWBI, which explicitly uses baseline-adjusted ANCOVA. So the missing EPDS baseline is a genuine feature of the published analysis, not obviously a defect of the Dryad deposit alone - though it is worth confirming whether the deposited dataset even contains an EPDS baseline variable at all. 3) covars_published=Pre_preg_BMI is NOT supported by the paper's statistical methods for either PGWBI or EPDS: prepregnancy BMI is used only as an inclusion criterion / descriptive baseline characteristic, never as a covariate in any reported between-group model (the only covariates used anywhere are the outcome's own prior-timepoint values, for PGWBI only). 4) arm_control=1 cannot be verified from the paper text, which never reports numeric codes for the 'Group' variable; this needs to be checked directly against the Dryad dataset/codebook. 5) Abstract states 'late pregnancy 72 (exercise 38, control 36)' which is arithmetically inconsistent (38+36=74, not 72); Table 2 clearly shows n=38 (exercise) and n=36 (control) analysed for the late-pregnancy PGWBI comparison, so we used 74 for n_analysed_primary. Postpartum numbers (36+34=70) are internally consistent.

analysis_method_quote: 'We analysed between-group differences in the effect of exercise training on psychological well-being (assessed by PGWBI) in late pregnancy and postpartum, and between-group difference in "Self-perceived general health status" in late pregnancy by general linear model analysis of covariance. Changes within-groups from baseline to late pregnancy and from late pregnancy to postpartum were also analysed by general linear model analysis of covariance. Baseline values of each outcome were set as covariates in late pregnancy analyses, and late pregnancy values were set as covariates in postpartum analyses. ... We analysed differences between groups in EPDS using an independent samples t-test. ... Due to the randomisation model, we assumed no systematic differences between groups at baseline. We based our primary analyses on the 'intention to treat' principle and additionally performed 'per protocol' analyses ... No adjustment for multiple testing have been undertaken.' (Methods, 'Statistical methods' section, p.3-4).
notes: This BMJ Open 2019 paper is a prespecified secondary analysis of the ETIP (Exercise Training in Pregnancy) RCT (NCT01243554); the ETIP trial's own primary outcome was gestational weight gain, reported in a different paper (Garnaes et al, PLoS Med 2016;13:e1002079, ref 32), not psychological well-being. Within THIS paper, no single outcome is formally declared 'primary' - candidates named in the abstract/introduction are (a) PGWBI global score (psychological well-being, late pregnancy and 3 months postpartum) and (b) EPDS total score (postnatal depression risk, 3 months postpartum). We coded PGWBI as primary_outcome_name per the task's default rule (first-named / most emphasised in the abstract), and documented EPDS as the secondary/additional outcome that our registry line actually tracks. EPDS results (Results 'Postnatal depression' paragraph, p.5-6; Table 2 does NOT include EPDS, only PGWBI and its 6 subscales): exercise 2.96 (95% CI 1.7 to 4.2) vs control 3.48 (95% CI 2.3 to 4.7), p=0.55 (independent samples t-test, postpartum value only, ITT); per-protocol EPDS: exercise 2.38 (95% CI 1.72 to 4.2) vs control 3.48 (95% CI 2.3 to 4.7), p=0.30. No EPDS baseline data are reported anywhere. PGWBI subscale-level and per-protocol results are in Table 2 and online supplementary table 1 (not extracted here since outside scope of primary outcome). IBM SPSS Statistics V.23 used; p<0.05 considered significant; explicitly no multiplicity correction across the many outcomes/subscales/timepoints tested. Randomisation used 'a computer random number generator' with no stratification factors mentioned in this paper (hence B_strat_factors_adjusted coded 'unclear').
